newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian lawyer says soldier shooting normal.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian lawyer says soldier shooting normal.

text.p: A lawyer defending a Jordanian soldier who gunned down Israeli seven schoolgirls said on Tuesday he had been provoked and any Arab would have reacted the same.

Ahmad Najdawi, the only lawyer to see Sergeant Ahmed al-Daqamsa since he emptied the clip of his rifle on March 13 at girls on a school trip to Baqoura, said the Israelis had insulted him while he performed prayers.
"They were making fun of him and that is for any person among us, any Moslem conducting prayers, when he sees such a situation, that in itself is sufficient to cause any explosion," Najdawi said.

"Ahmed al-Daqamsa belongs to this Arab nation, this Jordanian people, and what he has done could have been done by anyone in this nation, including me, if we were in his situation," Najdawi told reporters.

Leading Islamist and political opponents of the government are trying to whip up support for Daqamsa, who fired on the schoolgirls in a Jordanian border territory leased to Israel under the 1994 peace treaty.
The lawyer said a large legal counsel should be formed to defend his client, including volunteer lawyers from Arab countries.
He said he expected the government soon to issue charges against Daqamsa, who has been under military interrogation since his arrest immediately after the shooting.
Daqamsa's mother told reporters her family's house in the northern Jordanian town of Ibdr has been kept under tight surveillance and visitors only allowed in after identity card checks.
"There are always two to three police cars close to the house, and they even ask women who call on our house to bring their identity cards," Kamela Daqamsa, the soldier's mother said.

King Hussein said the killing was a shame on all Jordanians and flew to Israel to pay condolences to the victims' families. He later rebuked Daqamsa's army colleagues for not shooting him dead on the spot when be began firing.

Sympathisers of the soldier have indirectly criticised the king for comments they say prejudice the soldier's chances of a fair trial and demand Daqamsa has a public hearing where full legal safequards are applied.
